new.title: Climb to Sümela Monastery on its cliff face
new.desc: A Greek Orthodox monastery clinging to a cliff about 1,200 m above sea level in the Altındere valley, dedicated to the Virgin Mary and traditionally dated to the 4th century. Its rock-cut chapel and frescoed walls drew pilgrims for centuries until 1923.
new.tip: Go early to beat the coach groups and check the site is open before driving up, as restoration work has closed parts of it at times.
new.q: Sümela Manastırı, Altındere Vadisi Milli Parkı, Maçka, Trabzon

new.title: Find the ruined Vazelon Monastery in the forest
new.desc: A ruined Byzantine monastery near Maçka that Justinian I is said to have repaired in 565. Chapels, multi-storey rooms and traces of frescoes survive; the community left in 1923.
new.tip: The approach is a forest walk; wear proper shoes and ask in Maçka for current access.

new.title: See Uzungöl, the landslide lake among the pines
new.desc: A lake at about 1,250 m in Çaykara that formed when a landslide dammed a stream. Its shore is lined with wooden houses and trout restaurants, with forested peaks above.
new.tip: Sunrise and weekdays are far quieter than summer weekends; the loop path around the lake takes about an hour.

new.title: Walk up to Giresun Castle for the city and island view
new.desc: A hilltop castle site above Giresun with remains of old walls, a war-hero tomb and a wooded picnic area. From the summit you can see Giresun Island offshore.
new.tip: Reach it on foot or by car from the centre; late afternoon gives the best light over the sea.
new.q: Giresun Kalesi, Kapu, Giresun Merkez, Giresun

new.title: See the old stone houses of Zeytinlik
new.desc: Zeytinlik, once called Gogora, is Giresun's historic quarter of stone and timber houses built in the 19th century by Greek and Turkish families. It is a protected urban conservation area with about 80 registered houses.
new.tip: Combine it with the nearby museum; the lanes are steep, so wear flat shoes.

new.title: Visit Giresun Museum in the former Gogora church
new.desc: The museum occupies a Greek Orthodox church of the 1850s-60s and has been a museum since 1988, with archaeological and ethnographic finds from the region.
new.tip: Check opening hours at the entrance as they change seasonally; it is a short walk from the castle slope.
new.q: Giresun Müzesi, Zeytinlik, Giresun Merkez, Giresun

new.title: Visit the 17th-century Şeyh Keramettin Mosque
new.desc: A stone mosque on Gazi Street in central Giresun built in the early 17th century, with a wooden ceiling and a two-storey wooden gallery. A 1642 tax register already mentions it and the tomb beside it.
new.tip: Step in outside prayer times and look up at the wooden ceiling and gallery. Dress modestly.
new.q: Şeyh Keramettin Camii, Gazi Caddesi, Giresun Merkez, Giresun

new.title: Explore Tirebolu Castle on its seaside peninsula
new.desc: A castle on a headland above Tirebolu's harbour with a small chapel, a mosque remnant and Ottoman tombstones. Tirebolu grew from the ancient Tripolis, a Milesian trading colony.
new.tip: Pair it with a fish or pide lunch in the town; the hill gives views of the Harşit estuary.

new.title: See Eynesil Castle on its rocky peninsula
new.desc: A small coastal castle on a rock outcrop with a water cistern and a reported former church. It sits right on the sea road between Giresun and Trabzon.
new.tip: A short stop from the coast highway; take care on the rocks near the sea.

new.title: Climb to Andoz Castle above Espiye
new.desc: A small hilltop castle with walls and towers overlooking the sea and the Espiye valley.
new.tip: Allow a short uphill walk; combine with Espiye's pide houses.

new.title: Scale the cliff-top fortress of Şebinkarahisar
new.desc: A castle perched on a steep cliff above the town, with cisterns, rock-cut tombs and walls following the rock edge. The name Karahisar means black fortress.
new.tip: Allow an hour; the steps are steep and exposed.

new.title: Descend into Karaca Cave's dripstone halls
new.desc: A show cave in Cebeli village, Torul, found in 1983 and opened to visitors in 1996. About 105 m long, it has stalactites, stalagmites, columns and travertine pools in white to deep blue.
new.tip: Open roughly mid-April to mid-November; it is cool inside, so bring a layer.
new.q: Karaca Mağarası, Cebeli Köyü, Torul, Gümüşhane

new.title: Step out on the Torul glass terrace
new.desc: A 90 sq m glass platform about 240 m above the valley beside Torul Castle, built 2016-2018. The fortress is attributed to Genoese-era builders and was taken by the Ottomans in 1479.
new.tip: Not for those afraid of heights; weekends in summer bring queues.

new.title: Wander the abandoned Greek village of Santa
new.desc: A 17th-century Greek settlement in Dumanlı village near Gümüşhane, with stone houses and churches left empty after the 1923 population exchange.
new.tip: Free open-air site; the track is rough in places, so wear sturdy shoes.
new.q: Santa Köyü, Dumanlı, Gümüşhane Merkez, Gümüşhane

new.title: Tour Gümüşhane's İkizevler city museum
new.desc: A museum in two joined historic mansions of the Süleymaniye quarter, showing ethnographic displays of old Gümüşhane life.
new.tip: Check hours; fits well with a walk through the surrounding old quarter.
new.q: İkizevler Kent Müzesi, Süleymaniye, Gümüşhane Merkez, Gümüşhane

new.title: Picnic at Limni Gölü among pine and fir
new.desc: A lake in a nature park in Torul close to Zigana, ringed by pine and fir forest.
new.tip: An entrance fee applies; visit in summer, as snow can block the road for months.

new.title: Spend an afternoon at Sera Lake
new.desc: A small freshwater lake of about 14 hectares near Akçaabat with carp and barbel, plus crayfish introduced later. Fishing is allowed and there is a camping and picnic area.
new.tip: Reach it by the Akçaabat road and a short gravel stretch; bring food, as facilities are basic.

new.title: Hike the Altındere valley trails
new.desc: Altındere Valley National Park, declared in 1987, protects forested gorges and streams around Sümela Monastery, with walking paths and a forest road along the stream.
new.tip: Start from the park entrance below Sümela; trails are wet after rain.
new.q: Altındere Vadisi Milli Parkı, Maçka, Trabzon

new.title: Ski the slopes of Zigana winter sports centre
new.desc: A winter sports centre at about 2,050 m on the Torul boundary, declared in 1991 and the only ski resort of the eastern Black Sea. It has a short chairlift and two runs of roughly 600-800 m.
new.tip: Season depends on snow, usually from December; check conditions before driving up.
new.q: Zigana Kayak Merkezi, Zigana, Torul, Gümüşhane

new.title: Fly a tandem paraglide over Uzungöl
new.desc: Tandem flights launch from the slopes of Lustra plateau at around 2,000 m, with views of the lake, the plateaus and the Haldizen valley.
new.tip: Book with a licensed operator in Uzungöl; flights depend on wind and weather.

new.title: Join the Hıdırnebi plateau festival
new.desc: Hıdırnebi plateau at about 1,742 m above Akçaabat hosts a summer festival around 20-22 July, with a mineral spring nearby.
new.tip: Dates shift by year; the access road leaves the Akçaabat-Düzköy road.

new.title: Go to the Kadırga Festival on the treeless summit
new.desc: Kadırga plateau near Tonya, at the meeting point of several districts, hosts the region's best-known yayla festival each July, drawing very large crowds.
new.tip: Dates vary by year; arrive early as roads fill up.

new.title: Spend a day on Kümbet Plateau
new.desc: A highland above Dereli at roughly 1,700-1,900 m, known for flowers, forest, guesthouses and a Friday bazaar, with a major July festival.
new.tip: Dolmuş serve it in summer; the festival is around the second weekend of July.

new.title: Take a boat to Giresun Island
new.desc: Giresun Island, ancient Aretias, lies about 1.6 km offshore with ruins of walls and a monastery. Greeks reportedly held out here against the Ottomans until 1468.
new.tip: Boats leave from Giresun harbour in season.

new.title: Watch a Sürmene kama knife being made
new.desc: Sürmene knives and kamas have been forged in the town since at least Byzantine times; kama maker Cengizhan Alpaslan, third generation, works in the Soğuksu quarter and says a kama passes through some 72 steps.
new.tip: Call ahead, as only a handful of masters remain; beware imitations sold online.

new.title: Walk the Örümcek Forest of centuries-old firs
new.desc: A forest in Yeşilköy village, Kürtün, with fir and spruce trees over 400 years old, best from May to October.
new.tip: Distances are long from the coast; go in summer.

new.title: Eat baked Hamsiköy sütlaç in its home village
new.desc: Hamsiköy sütlacı, baked rice pudding from the Maçka highland, received a geographical indication in 2017. Tunç Sütlaç in the village centre is praised for its sugar-rice balance.
new.tip: The balcony is small; visit off-peak.

new.title: Try sac kavurma at Hamsiköy Taşlık
new.desc: A family restaurant in Çıralı, Hamsiköy, serving sac kavurma, kuru fasulye and pilaf.
new.tip: Order the sac kavurma, then sütlaç only if you have room.
new.q: Hamsiköy Taşlık Restaurant, Çıralı, Hamsiköy, Maçka, Trabzon

new.title: Eat hazelnut sütlaç at Garibin Yeri in Maçka
new.desc: A dessert place opposite the Sümela Otel on Atatürk Caddesi serving Hamsiköy sütlaç with hazelnuts, open late.
new.tip: Handy for those not driving up to Hamsiköy.
new.q: Hamsiköy Sütlacı Maçka Garibin Yeri, Atatürk Caddesi, Merkez, Maçka, Trabzon

new.title: Eat kuymak and a Black Sea breakfast at Salim Kafe
new.desc: A lakeside café on Manzara Caddesi in Uzungöl with hanging egg chairs and swings. Reviewers praise its serpme breakfast and kuymak.
new.tip: Come in the morning for the breakfast spread. It is busy at weekends, so arrive early.
new.q: Salim Kafe, Manzara Caddesi No:42, Uzungöl, Çaykara, Trabzon

new.title: Order Giresun yağlısı pide at Turhanlar
new.desc: A pide house on Bekirpaşa Caddesi known for the classic Giresun yağlısı, a butter-rich pide, plus kıymalı and kuşbaşılı versions.
new.tip: Go at lunch for fresh pide from the oven.
new.q: Turhanlar Pide, Bekirpaşa Caddesi No:12, Kapu, Giresun Merkez, Giresun

new.title: Eat buttery Görele pide at Sahil Pide
new.desc: A wood-fired pide house on Görele's seafront known for its closed kıymalı pide topped with an egg and plenty of butter.
new.tip: Start with the kıymalı kapalı.
new.q: Sahil Pide Salonu, Dr. Erdem Dülger Bulvarı, Hendekbaşı, Görele, Giresun

new.title: Eat tel kadayıf at Meşhur Tel Kadayıfçı
new.desc: A Giresun sweet shop on Fatih Caddesi making tel kadayıf, a dessert of the hazelnut country.
new.tip: Pair with Turkish tea in the afternoon.
new.q: Meşhur Tel Kadayıfçı, Fatih Caddesi No:21/B, Giresun Merkez, Giresun

new.title: Try Ardasa siron kebab at Ataç Konağı
new.desc: Ardasa siron kebabı, a Gümüşhane dish combining meat with siron, a traditional bakery product, is served at Ataç Konağı.
new.tip: Book ahead on weekends.
